definition: A key performance indicator (KPI) is a measurable value used to assess progress toward a specific business objective.
extendedDefinition: A KPI connects a business objective to a metric that can be reviewed over a defined period. A useful KPI has a clear formula, data source, owner, target, and review cadence; a number without those definitions can be misleading. Teams should distinguish leading indicators, which may signal future outcomes, from lagging indicators that report what already happened. When choosing analytics or reporting software, confirm that the tool can calculate the metric consistently, explain filters and attribution, and let the intended users act on the result. Avoid tracking dozens of metrics without a decision attached to each one.
examples: A support team sets a target to resolve 80% of tickets within one business day and tracks the percentage weekly.
A SaaS business monitors monthly recurring revenue alongside trial-to-paid conversion to understand both current revenue and the pipeline feeding it.
A product team tracks activation within seven days of signup as a leading indicator, then checks whether activated users retain better after 30 and 90 days.
description: A KPI is a defined metric tied to a business goal. Learn how to set measurable targets, choose useful leading and lagging indicators, and verify that reporting tools calculate them consistently.
